The patient’s renal function and proteinuria were regularly monitored at a nephrology department, and medication for hypertension (losartan) was attempted as a treatment to decrease the proteinuria.

clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient exhibited a classic lifelong progression of alkaptonuria with multisystemic ochronosis. Since childhood, characteristic black spots were noted on underpants and bed sheets (E001). In his early 40s, pigmentation of the sclera, ears, and fingers developed, with ophthalmologic evaluation documenting scleral discolouration but failing to establish a diagnosis (E002). During his late 40s, he developed chronic cough with peripheral eosinophilia and reduced lung function (60%), raising suspicion for eosinophilic asthma (E003). In his early 50s, incidental proteinuria was detected, prompting nephrology monitoring and treatment with losartan for hypertension, with differential diagnoses including renal cancer and glomerulonephritis considered (E004). Musculoskeletal symptoms progressed from knee problems in his 50s to diffuse lower back, groin, and hip pain, eventually requiring total hip arthroplasty where distinctive black discolouration of the femoral head was observed (E005, E009). Spinal cysts were also identified on high-resolution CT (E008). The diagnostic breakthrough occurred in his early 70s when his monozygotic twin brother underwent surgery revealing black bone tissue intraoperatively, prompting termination of the procedure (E006). This triggered a diagnostic triad comprising urine spot testing for homogentisic acid (positive in both brothers) and genetic testing, which identified heterozygous pathogenic variants c.481G>A and c.1017G>T in the HGD gene, confirming the diagnosis (E007).
